He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]] before playing parts of four [[NBA]] seasons for the [[Washington Wizards]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Chicago Bulls]] and [[Boston Celtics]], totalling 34 games between 2015 to 2018. He went on to build a career overseas. In 2019, he helped lead French club [[SIG Strasbourg]] to a LNB Pro A [[Leaders Cup]] championship while, in 2023–24, he captured both a Romanian League and Romanian Cup championship with [[U-BT Cluj-Napoca]], the latter competition being named MVP. His career includes stops in Spain, Turkey, Greece, Puerto Rico and Saudi Arabia. ==High school career== Eddie attended the [[Cannon School]] in [[Concord, North Carolina]], where he was a five-year letter winner for coach Ron Johnson. He scored 2,600 points in his high school career and was an all-conference selection all five years. He was also an all-state selection as a sophomore, junior and senior.{{cite web | url=http://www.hokiesports.com/mbasketball/players/eddie_jarell.html | title=31 Jarell Eddie | work=HokieSports.com | access-date=November 4, 2014 | archive-date=March 3, 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180303225214/http://www.hokiesports.com/mbasketball/players/eddie_jarell.html | url-status=dead }} As a junior in 2008–09, he averaged 25 points and 8 rebounds per game while leading the Cougars to a co-conference championship in its first year in the Charlotte Independent Schools Athletic Association (CISAA).{{cite web | url=http://www.cannonschool.org/page/News-Detail?pk=513747 | title=Media Advisory: National Letter of Intent Signing Ceremony – Basketball Standout Jarell Eddie (Virginia Tech) | work=CannonSchool.org | date=November 9, 2009 | access-date=December 29, 2015 | archive-date=March 4, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083204/http://www.cannonschool.org/page/News-Detail?pk=513747 | url-status=dead }} In November 2009, Eddie signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college basketball]] for [[Virginia Tech]]. He went on to participate in the 2010 [[Capital Classic (all-star game)|Capital Classic]], and was ranked nationally #63 by Rivals.com and #77 by Scout.com. ==College career== As a freshman at [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] in 2010–11, Eddie had a subdued role as he averaged just 2.9 points, 2.2 rebounds and 10.9 minutes in 27 games (no starts). He later missed the postseason due to a violation of team rules.{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/jarell-eddie-1.html | title=Jarell Eddie Stats | work=Sports-Reference.com | access-date=November 4, 2014}} As a sophomore in 2011–12, Eddie appeared in all 33 games with 32 starting assignments. He ranked third on the team in scoring at 9.1 points per game and led the team in scoring on four occasions. He also led the team in three-pointers made (54), three-point percentage (44.3) and free-throw percentage (86.8). In addition, he averaged 4.8 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game. As a junior in 2012–13, Eddie was named to the ACC All-Academic team. In 32 games (28 starts), he averaged 12.3 points, 5.6 rebounds and 1.3 assists in 30.3 minutes per game. As a senior in 2013–14, Eddie was named to the ACC All-Academic team for the second straight year. On December 9, 2013, he was named the ACC Player of the Week after he led the Hokies to a pair of wins, including a 61–60 overtime road victory against the defending ACC champion [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami]]. He scored 24 points against Miami and a career-high 34 points in an 81–63 win over [[Winthrop Eagles men's basketball|Winthrop]].{{cite web |
